title: 7th special sitting of 2025
summary: The Majlis held a special sitting outside its normal term to finish work on the Maldives Media and Broadcasting Regulation Bill, put forward by independent member Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru of Thulhaadhoo. The Independent Institutions Committee's report was presented and debated, with PNC members backing it and opposition members objecting to the pace and lack of wider consultation. Several members were ordered out of the chamber for disorder. Four amendments passed and the bill passed its final vote 60-1.

Attendance of members

items.title: Chair's announcement: special sitting outside the term to finish the Media and Broadcasting Regulation Bill
items.outcome: announced; sitting convened at the request of signing members

items.title: Committee report on the Maldives Media and Broadcasting Regulation Bill (Independent Institutions Committee)
Votes on amendments and on the bill (third reading)

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: As the bill's sponsor, argued Article 27 of the constitution ties free expression to Islamic principles; urged members to pass the bill.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said the committee addressed media concerns and the commission appointment process has no presidential role.
Argued the bill does not restrict social media use by young people.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Moved amendments to clauses 13, 21(n), 45(r) and 39(v) of the bill.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Backed the bill, saying media can be regulated within the constitution and Islamic principles, and said he would vote to pass it.

speakers.name: Ahmed Saleem
positions: Called for orderly, respectful conduct in the chamber and argued the bill is worth debating despite opposition discontent.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Said he disagreed with the committee outcome and urged more time and consultation with media bodies and human rights institutions; said he would not vote for it.
Raised a point of order on a reply made to his remarks.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Argued the sitting breached the rules because the committee report and agenda reached members late.
Said the PNC supermajority was being used to push the bill through.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Seconded the amendments to clause 13 and clause 39(v).

speakers.name: Hussain Riza Adam
positions: Presented the committee report: written views sought from agencies and the public, bill passed at the committee's 36th meeting.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Argued the bill is aimed at curbing reporting on alleged government corruption and warned of tighter control of the press.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Seconded the amendment to clause 21(n) on how media vote in the commission selection.

speakers.name: Ismail Nizar
positions: Seconded the amendment to clause 45(r) on exempt publications.

decisions: Seven members were ordered out of the chamber for breaching the rules of conduct (South Hithadhoo, South Galolhu, Keyodhoo, North Galolhu, South Hulhumale', Kendhoo, Vaikaradhoo).
Two amendments from the South Galolhu member were not put to a vote because he had been ordered out of the chamber.
Amendment to clause 13 (transfer of assets, agreements and registrations to the new commission) passed.
Amendment to clause 21(n) (registered broadcasters and media vote under Elections Commission rules, one vote each) passed.
Amendment to clause 45(r) (exemption for publications of parties, clubs, unions and similar bodies for their own members) passed.
Amendment to clause 39 adding a ban on spreading news that harms children's rights passed.
The Maldives Media and Broadcasting Regulation Bill passed with the amendments, 60-1.
Chair sent the Sergeant-at-Arms report on committee guests' conduct to the General Committee to amend the rules, and referred damage to a committee-room sound system to the conduct committee.

votes.what: Amendment to clause 13 (transitional provisions), moved by Mohamed Mamdooh
Amendment to clause 21(n) (media voting in commission selection)
Amendment to clause 39 (news harming children's rights)
Maldives Media and Broadcasting Regulation Bill, third reading, as amended
